capex.item: Electron beam cold hearth remelting/refining furnace with capacity in excess of 5000 tonnes/year to recycle scrap titanium into aerospace-grade material.
capex.quote: the bigger capacity that we have bought is the electron beam cold hard re-melting furnace ... And that's a capacity in excess of 5000 tons per year

capex.item: Vacuum arc remelting (VAR) line for titanium ingots/billets with capacity of around 1500 tonnes/year.
capex.quote: even though this has a capacity of around 1500 tons per year

capex.item: Vacuum induction melting (VIM) equipment for superalloy raw materials with annual capacity of around 600 tonnes, using a 1000 kg furnace for special/intricate alloys.
capex.quote: Again, an annual capacity of around 600 tons to make rock materials for VIM ... We have gone for only a 1000 kg furnace

capex.item: Adding 300 tonnes/year of titanium casting capacity at the new 50-acre facility, via a large titanium casting furnace with over 400 kg metric melt capacity.
capex.quote: For titanium castings, we are adding a capacity of 300 tons ... with an annual capacity of over 300 tons of titanium castings

capex.item: Adding 300 tonnes/year of superalloy casting capacity (via a vacuum induction moulding furnace up to 1000 kg), taking combined new aerospace casting capacity to 600 tonnes/year.
capex.quote: One is 300 tons for titanium casting and 300 tons for superalloy casting. So, combined together 600 tons annual capacity

capex.item: Capex for the aerospace castings part of about INR 150 crore, of which only INR 10-15 crore has been spent so far.
capex.quote: The casting part is another INR150 crores ... That spend is not started much. That will be only INR10 crores to INR15 crores

capex.item: Capex for the aerospace materials (titanium/superalloy metal) plant of about INR 170-180 crore, of which roughly INR 65-80 crore already spent.
capex.quote: the capex for the materials part of our business is, in the tune of around ... INR170 crores to INR180 crores. And out of that, a capex of around INR80 crores, INR65 crores is already done

capex.item: Setting up a separate plant to assemble, fabricate and weld complete M777 ultra-lightweight howitzer titanium structures, using equipment relocated from BAE's shut UK plant.
capex.quote: we have signed up with these systems to not just make the castings but assemble and fabricate and weld them together to make the entire structures for the gun, for the M777 ULH, which is a big thing for which a separate plant is being set up

credit.rationale: Ratings upgraded reflecting expected improvement in scale of operations, earnings profile and product diversity, supported by successful commissioning of key titanium and superalloy expansion assets (VAR, VIM, plasma arc melting) and enhanced order visibility in aerospace, defence and space propulsion segments. | Operating income of Rs. 308.1 crore in FY2025 is expected to more than double over FY2026 and FY2027, aided by increased business under subsidiary Aerolloy Technologies (ATL) and scale-up of Trac Precision Solutions (TPSL, acquired December 2024). | Financial risk profile remains comfortable and liquidity strong, supported by equity raises that strengthened net worth; planned capex of Rs. 500 crore over FY2026-FY2028 to be funded via a mix of debt and internal accruals, with project execution and scale-up remaining key monitorables.

business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- Framed around a stated 'dharma' of 'Building Parity' - helping India stand at par with the world in capability, technology, knowledge, quality, skill, workmanship and talent, extended to productivity, efficiency and sustainability.
- Describes its core manufacturing technologies as 'platform-independent', covering 360 degrees across the entire A&D sector: Civil Aviation, Air Defence, Aero Engines, Space, Land Defence, Naval Defence and Strategic Systems.
- Chairman cites programme wins and partnerships with Blue Origin, Honeywell Aerospace Technologies, Safran Aircraft Engines, ISRO-VSSC and BrahMos Aerospace as reinforcing India's self-reliance in critical aerospace-grade materials.
- Deepening engagement with Blue Origin on the BE-4 engine programme - development and supply of flight-critical material, extending Aerolloy's qualified-supplier footprint in space propulsion hardware.
- Presented PTC-Aerolloy's integrated Titanium and Superalloy platform (melt, casting, forging and mill products) at TITANIUM Europe 2026 in Toulouse, France in April 2026, engaging global OEMs, producers and industry leaders.

open.item: Carbon-footprint roadmap: measure Scope 1 and 2 in 2023, define reduction plan in 2024, measure Scope 3 by 2025, and take a global leadership role in carbon reduction from 2026.
Foreign OEM/export business to move from domestic-heavy today to a balanced, roughly equal split with domestic over the next three to four years.
Aerospace and defence business to grow from 15-20% of revenue today to 70-80% of total revenue over the next five years.
Aerospace castings plus aerospace materials segment to rise to over 70% of total revenue in the next five years.
Adding 300 tonnes/year of titanium casting capacity at the new 50-acre facility, via a large titanium casting furnace with over 400 kg metric melt capacity.
Adding 300 tonnes/year of superalloy casting capacity (via a vacuum induction moulding furnace up to 1000 kg), taking combined new aerospace casting capacity to 600 tonnes/year.
Capex for the aerospace materials (titanium/superalloy metal) plant of about INR 170-180 crore, of which roughly INR 65-80 crore already spent.
Capex for the aerospace castings part of about INR 150 crore, of which only INR 10-15 crore has been spent so far.
Electron beam cold hearth remelting/refining furnace with capacity in excess of 5000 tonnes/year to recycle scrap titanium into aerospace-grade material.
Vacuum arc remelting (VAR) line for titanium ingots/billets with capacity of around 1500 tonnes/year.
Vacuum induction melting (VIM) equipment for superalloy raw materials with annual capacity of around 600 tonnes, using a 1000 kg furnace for special/intricate alloys.
Green titanium via cold hearth recycling to cut carbon emissions by over 130,000 tonnes annually at full 5000-tonne capacity (~26 tonnes CO2 saved per tonne of recycled titanium).
New 50-acre facility to source almost 50% of its power from renewable sources (solar).
Setting up a separate plant to assemble, fabricate and weld complete M777 ultra-lightweight howitzer titanium structures, using equipment relocated from BAE's shut UK plant.
Titanium sponge supply is a future risk as most sponge production is in ex-CIS/Russia/China/Japan and the Russia-Ukraine war has squeezed supply.

themes.title: Commercial-aerospace supply chain (Boeing/Airbus/engine OEMs)
themes.need: A record global commercial-aircraft backlog plus engine-OEM (GE/Safran/Honeywell/RR/P&W) outsourcing and China+1 are pulling Indian build-to-print suppliers up the value chain - aero-engine hot-section airfoils, airframe structures, tooling and wire harnesses. AZAD ramping engine/airfoil exports; UNIMECH near-tripling tooling capacity; AEQUS/SANSERA on precision aero; ROSSTECH on harnesses; PTCIL on titanium castings.
themes.driver: New commercial-aero RFP wins; engine-component capacity ramps; new MRO licences; Boeing/Airbus build-rate recovery.
